items.title: 61520_Teddy Edwards oral history interview
items.q: I also had heard Billie Holiday for my first time at the Paradise Theatre... Also, out on the south end... that's where I heard Billie Holiday again.

ctx.x: I also had heard Billie Holiday for my first time at the Paradise Theatre, and I heard Sarah Vaughan the first time at the Paradise Theatre. The first time she came to Detroit with Fatha Hines, they were playing two pianos back to back, two pianos on the stage, and she was playing and he was playing -- there were two white pianos sitting out in front of the band. And they really used to do show business(?) up. It was really something.

One of my favorite ladies that I saw at the Graystone Ballroom was Miss Lil Green. She had the big hits out, "In The Dark" and "I Want To Copyright Your Love" and all those things. And she'd just stand up there and just let it just roll out, you know. She didn't do any body movements at all. She'd just stand up there and let the sounds come out, you know. But she would talk plenty of stuff. She talked plenty of street talk in those songs. Later on some years, I worked with Peggy Lee and Benny Goodman, and we…
